This role owns the data side of that mission: the models, pipelines, and analysis that make cost, usage, and margin numbers trustworthy across the company. This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the dbt model or Python pipeline that ships the fix, building the cost-vs-revenue mart that answers a margin question once instead of every time, and chasing a number until it reconciles. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case or a data model's implications to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week. What You'll Be Responsible For In this role, you'll: - Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. jobs.title: Head of New Media
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Traditional PR is fading — we go directly to our audience. This role brings together what used to be two separate seats, communications and social media, into one mid-to-senior, hands-on role: owning Supabase's voice in the channels where developers actually pay attention, and building our founders' presence in them. "New media" here means modern and direct, not traditional press — we care far more about getting our founders onto the right podcasts and YouTube channels than landing a New York Times placement. It's part comms, part social operator, with a sharper edge than a typical polite PR hire: someone willing to put an opinion out there and push a little rather than always play it safe. But it's not just a social media job either — this person also needs the poise and technical credibility to lead comms through genuinely high-stakes moments, like a major incident, where reporters, investors, and customers all need a calm, credible, technically fluent voice at the same time. jobs.title: Container Engineer
jobs.description_text: More than 9 million developers and 250,000+ customers now build on Supabase, and the majority of new databases on the platform are created by AI app builders — so the systems underneath have to stay reliable while they grow fast. ABOUT THE ROLE Container Engineering (ConEng) owns the internal container platform that runs Supabase's multi-tenant, multi-region services — the managed Kubernetes platform that other engineering teams build and deploy on top of. We own cluster lifecycle and cluster classes, multi-cluster and multi-region topology, capacity, scheduling, isolation and runtime safety, the higher-level platform APIs, the Kubernetes deployment contract and Argo semantics, rollout primitives, and runtime configuration and secret injection. Your job is to make the platform itself trustworthy, observable, and cheap to operate at scale — and to raise the reliability bar for everyone who depends on it. This is not a gatekeeper role. You'll make the reliable path the easy path: building the automation and platform APIs that let product teams run safely by default, instrumenting what we operate, and making sure that when something breaks we detect it and recover fast. The work spans three strength areas: Tooling & ecosystem — deep knowledge of the container and orchestration landscape (Kubernetes, containerd/OCI, the CNCF ecosystem) and a clear point of view on how to compose it. Software engineering — designing and building the platform's automation, controllers, and internal

The AI Tooling team runs its own services in production and carries its own on-call. Traffic from AI clients and agents behaves differently from traffic from people: hundreds of calls a minute, retry loops, and no reading of deprecation warnings. This role makes sure the services they use are reliable, correctly authorized and observable. It is a systems and infrastructure role rather than a product AI role, and it is not an SRE role. You will build and operate these systems, not only advise on them. jobs.description_text: About the Role We’re looking for a Product Manager, Administration & Governance to join our Product Team and make Supabase the default starting point for software built inside a company. Inside most companies, Supabase starts the same way: someone has an idea, creates a project, and builds something useful. You’ll own how companies run Supabase as their internal development platform: approved by IT and easy for anyone in the company to use. You’ll make it possible for people and the agents they work with to start building without waiting on infrastructure, while giving platform, IT, and security teams the controls they need to say yes. The goal is to make the approved path the easiest path, from an early experiment to a production application, with the controls companies need built in. jobs.title: Senior AI/ML Engineer
jobs.description_text: About the role: We’re looking for a Senior AI/ML Engineer who will be working at the intersection of LLMs, real-time signal processing, and enterprise decision-making. This is not a research role or an isolated AI team position. You’ll sit alongside domain engineers as you ship production AI systems to enterprise customers. This is not the typical AI/ML engineering role. We’re looking for someone who uses AI heavily in their own daily work, has built and shipped features powered by LLMs and autonomous agents, and has strong opinions on what good AI product engineering actually looks like. If your go-to move when facing a complex problem is to reach for an agent pipeline rather than a static script, you’re the kind of engineer we have in mind. You’ll initially pair with our external AI partners to absorb their work and establish the patterns the broader engineering team will follow. jobs.description_text: About the Role We are looking for a Hardware Diagnostics Engineer to run burn-in, triage what fails, work servers out-of-band, and own RMAs end to end. If you like hardware that misbehaves in ways that take real work to explain, this is a good seat. Before any GPU server carries a customer workload, it has to prove it works — under load, at temperature, for hours. When it doesn't, somebody has to figure out why, get replacement hardware in, and send the failed part back to the vendor. What You’ll Do - Run server and GPU burn-in and stress testing, interpret the results, and decide whether hardware is production-ready - Triage failures across GPUs, memory, drives, NICs, PSUs, and cabling: reproduce the failure, isolate the faulty component, and document what proved it - Work servers out-of-band through IPMI and Redfish for power control, boot configuration, BIOS settings, and sensor and event log collection - Apply firmware updates across the fleet following the team's qualified baselines and rollout process - Drive RMAs with vendors from ticket through replacement, installation, and return of the failed part - Keep asset, serial, and replacement history accurate in NetBox so we know what's actually in every rack - Track failure patterns across the fleet and raise them when the same part or firmware version keeps turning up - Improve the runbooks you work from, and script the steps you find yourself repeating - Partner with datacenter operations on hands-on work during turn-up

You'll set the bar for what validated hardware means here, build the tooling that enforces it, and be the person we escalate to when a failure doesn't make sense. Firmware is where a lot of our hardest problems live. A BIOS revision changes how a GPU enumerates. A BMC update fixes one thing and breaks telemetry. jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.description_text: ABOUT TESSERA LABS Tessera Labs is a new category of enterprise software: an AI platform that changes how the world's largest companies run. Every large enterprise carries the same weight — decades of accumulated process, data, and code that no longer match the business it has become. Changing any of it is a program measured in years and hundreds of millions of dollars, staffed by armies of consultants, and it fails more often than anyone admits. Most companies have quietly accepted this as the cost of being large. We don't. Tessera is a transformation engine: a governed, multi-agent platform that understands an enterprise's process, data, and code as one connected system and changes it in weeks rather than years. We're vendor-agnostic by design — SAP, Salesforce, Workday, Oracle, Snowflake, MuleSoft — and tied to none of them. Two things make this hard, and they're the reason the job is interesting. Governance: every action is logged, traceable, and reversible, because our customers are regulated and these are the systems that close their books. And generality: the platform has to work on landscapes it has never seen, at companies whose complexity is genuinely unique to them. We sell a product, not a service. Our people are here to make the product successful, not the other way around. If you've watched enterprise AI companies quietly become consultancies, that distinction is the one to press us on. We raised a $60M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Foundation Capita

Your mission is to evolve this architecture so that open, multi-format data lakes are not just searchable by humans, but inherently AI-ready by transforming interoperable metadata into the contextual engine that powers agentic innovation.
